title: Reservation Onramp: SLA banding, GPU fit, and scaling policy intake
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Purpose: Create a repeatable onramp (front-door) for enterprise reserved capacity requests that standardizes SLA bands, maps workload profiles to GPU class recommendations, and defines scaling and burst policies. This ticket captures the product-level requirements, acceptance criteria, and rollout steps needed to deliver an intake + prioritization rubric that Sales, Solutions, and the Capacity team can use to accelerate deals without overcommitting capacity.

Scope:
- Define 3 SLA bands (A/B/C) with p95/p99 latency targets, throughput guarantees, and burst allowances.
- Produce a GPU-fit matrix mapping common workload archetypes (chat, long-form generation, embedding pipelines, reranking) to GPU classes (T4/GPU-small, A10/A30, A100-40/80GB, H100) with recommended reservation sizes.
- Formalize scaling policy templates: autoscale thresholds, cold-start constraints, burst-credit buckets, and preemption fallback behaviors.
- Draft an intake form with mandatory telemetry fields (expected QPS, sequence length distribution, 99th token latency SLO target, traffic seasonality, privacy/regulatory constraints).
- Define a prioritization score (0-100) combining business impact, technical fit, revenue velocity, and capacity risk to gate Dedicated commitments.

Sample SLA band definitions (working draft):
- Band A (Premium Enterprise): p99 < 150ms for interactive chat workloads at planned sustained throughput (e.g., 500 tokens/s); reserved throughput billed monthly; burst allowance up to 2x sustained for 30 minutes/day; recommended GPU class: H100 or A100-80 with dedicated KV/cache sharding.
- Band B (High Availability): p95 < 300ms, p99 < 600ms for batch/low-interactive workloads; reserved throughput with smaller burst window (1.5x for 15 minutes); recommended GPU class: A100-40 or A30.
- Band C (Cost-Optimized): best-effort latency with throughput floor guaranteed (e.g., 100 tokens/s); burst handled via queued requests and soft-fallback to lower-capacity regions; recommended GPU class: A10/T4.

GPU fit examples (decision heuristics):
- Short-turn chat (<1k tokens, many simultaneous users): prefer H100/A100 with KV cache dedication.
- Long-context generation (10k+ tokens, lower concurrency): prioritize VRAM (80GB) models, recommend A100-80 or H100 with sequence-parallel configuration.
- Embedding-heavy pipelines with streaming batched inference: prioritize throughput per GPU; A30 or A100-40 with large batch scheduling.

Trade-offs and risks:
- Aggressive SLA commitments increase reserved capacity cost and underutilization risk; propose a 30-day probation and usage review before hard SLA enforcement.
- Preferring top-tier GPUs reduces latency variance but increases price and sales friction; include standardized discount tiers and overage rules in contracts.
- Autoscaling is limited by model init times and KV cache warmup; scaling policy must include pre-warm windows and staged rollouts.

Deliverables:
- Intake form template (Google Form + internal Confluence intake page).
- Prioritization rubric spreadsheet with scoring formulas.
- GPU-fit matrix artifact and playbook text for Sales enablement.
- Acceptance criteria checklist and a 30/60-day review runbook.

Owners and stakeholders: PM (Aisha Patel), Capacity lead (Miguel Torres), Lead SWE (Jordan Li), Solutions Eng (Rina Gupta), Sales Engineering liaison (Ethan Cole).

This ticket is intentionally scoped to product-level decisions and artifacts. Implementation of automated recommendations and capacity placement routing will be separate ENG tickets after the rubric is approved.
acceptance_criteria: Published Confluence intake page with embedded form and example filled request
Prioritization rubric spreadsheet: contains at least 8 scoring fields, produces reproducible score
GPU-fit matrix covering 6 common workload archetypes with clear recommended GPU class and reservation ranges
Three SLA band definitions published and signed off by Sales, Solutions, and Capacity leads
Rollout checklist and 30/60-day monitoring template for committed customers

decision_notes: Adopt three-band SLA model (A/B/C) to balance commercial clarity with engineering enforcement.
Use score-based prioritization that factors revenue velocity and capacity risk; threshold 65+ to qualify for Concierge onboarding.
Require a minimum 30-day probationary observation window before elevating to contract SLA enforcement.
